0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard. was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 November 1973, after the draft finalized by the Switchgeax Sectional Committee had been approved by the and Controlgear Electrotechnical Division Council. ' Dot:
0.2 assistance has been derived from In preparing this standard, 16 ( Central Office) 29 and 35 ` Draft Recommendations for standard direction of movement for control devices operating electrical apparatus ' issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. 0.3 This standard is aimed at standardizing, in systems employing electrical apparatus, the relationship between the direction of the manual action applied to the control device and the final effect requirecl by this This is of particular value where safety is concerned and is action. specially important where a wrong operating movement may cause damage or where stress is laid on a high operating speed, as for example, in applications involving intermittent drive, such as cranes, trucks and other transport vehicles. This standard the general public. will also be useful for devices the likely moving to be operated direction of by the

0.4 The term operating direction implies hand, when operating the control device.

OS It is fully recognized that standard rules for ~direction of motion cannot be strictly applicable under all circumstances. In many cases, the suitable direction of motion will necessarily depend upon particular conditions of construction and mounting which cannot be foreseen or specified in general rules. 0.5.1 Sometimes a standard direction meaning, as in the~case of a revolving either end, or a two-way switch. will be undeterminable or have no shaft fitted with a handwheel at rules will

0.5.2 It is evident therefore, that exceptions to the standard occur and shall, therefore, be permitted when required. 3

IS : 7118- 1973 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers recommendations for standard direction of movement for control devices operating electrical apparatus and is applicable to manually operated devices, such as, handwheels, handles, rods and cord, which control the knobs, grips, levers, push-buttons, operation of electrical apparatus, such as regulating resistors, controllers The electrical apparatus so operated may comprise a and switches. complete functional unit, or may be a component part of a larger assembl) of electrical or nonelectrical equipment, for example, motor, pump This standard also applies to servomotors and the steering and fluidvane. of certain types of electric trucks.
1.2 Additional requirements manual controls. 2. PRINCIPLE may be necessary for controls other than

OF IDENTIFICATION

2.1 The
general applied

object of this standard is to enable the operator to foresee in cases, the direction of the effect, which results from an action in a given direction to the control device.

2.1.1 The control devices may be of very different forms, such as grips, As a rule, however, they handwheels, knurled knobs and push-buttons. can only move in one or the other of two opposed directions, for example, motion from left to right or from right to left, from back to front or front to back and rotation clockwise or anticlockwise. 2.1.2 This standard takes into account, for the most current cases, both the direction of action on the control device, and the final effect intended on the apparatus being operated and classify them in two groups for the most usual cases (see Table 1 ), it being understood that, unlecs the convention specified in Table 1, should cause serious disadvantages, any effect belonging to Group 1 shall be obtained by an action classified in Group 1, any effect belonging to Group 2 shall be obtained by an action classified in Group 2. 2.2 Table 2 gives typical examples of control devices and recommended operating directions. The operating direction is understood to be determined by a person standing at the operating place, for instance, where the figure number is placed in the examples of `Table 2. 2.3 When, for some imperative reason, such as, an existing and widespread practice, these rules cannot be applied, it is particularly recommended that the control devices shall be provided with labels or other indications, specifying clearly the direction of the effect correspondillg to the action on the device. NOTE - In the case of doubt of the final effect of the operation, the nature of this effect shouid be indicated on the operating device (for e-ample, on sever-a! similar
controllers of one opera&g post ).

RECOMMENDATZONS

3.1 To move an object in direction other than shorvn in Table 1, the hand should be moved essentially in the direction of the movement desired of the object. 3.2 To lift or to lo\vcr au object by means of a lever, for \vhich the motion of the hand is practically horizontal, a practice contrary to the recommendation given in Table 1 is usual ( see Fig. 1 ).

This rule applies to control devices associated with electrical appliances which dare only operated occasionally and which are important with regard to safety. It does not apply to control devices intended to be operated by skilled persons in those cases where a convenient operation is of great importance, for example, dead man's button on a lever and levers for controllers.
